title: Initialize Express.js + TypeScript backend
description: Set up a separate backend package (server/) inside the monorepo using Express.js and TypeScript. The server should start on PORT from environment, have structured routing, global error handling, and a health check endpoint.
acceptanceCriteria: server/ directory exists with its own package.json and tsconfig.json
Running 'npm run dev' in server/ starts the Express server with ts-node-dev hot reload
GET /api/health returns { status: 'ok', timestamp: ISO string }
TypeScript compiles without errors via 'npm run build'
Global error handler returns JSON error responses (not HTML)
Request logging is enabled via morgan

steps.description: Create server/ directory and initialize package.json
steps.details: Run: mkdir server && cd server && npm init -y. Install dependencies: npm install express cors helmet morgan dotenv. Install dev dependencies: npm install -D typescript @types/node @types/express @types/cors @types/morgan ts-node-dev.

Create server/tsconfig.json: { compilerOptions: { target: 'ES2020', module: 'commonjs', lib: ['ES2020'], outDir: './dist', rootDir: './src', strict: true, esModuleInterop: true, skipLibCheck: true, resolveJsonModule: true }, include: ['src/**/*'], exclude: ['node_modules', 'dist'] }

Create server/src/index.ts that: imports dotenv/config, creates Express app, applies morgan('dev') logging middleware, applies cors() with FRONTEND_URL from env, applies express.json(), mounts routes at /api, adds global error handler (4 params: err, req, res, next), starts listening on process.env.PORT || 3000.
Create server/src/routes/health.ts with a router that handles GET / returning { status: 'ok', timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }. Mount it in index.ts at /api/health.

Create server/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts that accepts (err: Error, req, res, next) and returns res.status(err.status || 500).json({ error: err.message || 'Internal server error' }). Create a custom AppError class with status and message.

steps.description: Verify server starts and health check works
steps.details: Run 'npm run dev' in server/. Then run: curl http://localhost:3000/api/health — should return {"status":"ok","timestamp":"..."}. Verify a bad route returns JSON error, not HTML.

technicalNotes: Use ts-node-dev instead of nodemon for TypeScript hot-reload without a separate compile step
The CORS middleware must be applied before routes to ensure preflight OPTIONS requests work
Global error handler must have exactly 4 parameters for Express to recognize it as an error handler
